name: Flat Vector Illustration, a supplemental design reference in the Drawing and Illustration category. The source does not present it as a directly named style, and SVG use does not establish this aesthetic.
visualIdentity: Clear flat color fields, simplified figures, and consistent corner radii, using three to five main colors plus one fixed accent. Icons, outlines, and typography stay proportionally consistent. Avoid photorealistic reflections, complex materials, and inconsistent shadows.
suitableUses: Explicitly, the source says this style stands alone for most explainers and brand pieces. Inferred from its combinations, it also suits product feature tours and flat data scenes. Character scenes fit only when the artwork has readable eyes or a rig.
limitations: Photorealistic reflections, complex materials, and inconsistent shadows are excluded. Body text should not sit on the accent_1 or accent_2 fills, which fail the 4.5 contrast target. Gaze-following needs separate eye layers or a rig. Suggested details were not verified in the source video.
palette: Suggested, not supplied: background #F7F3E9, foreground #243746, accent_1 #267D82, accent_2 #DD7353 as the fixed coral emphasis, and accent_3 #EAC664. Gradients are disabled. Foreground on background (11.083) and foreground on accent_3 (7.462) meet body-text targets. Task-supplied colors override these values.
motionAndInteraction: For video, all state derives from composition time, using authored easing where it helps. Deliberate cuts, impacts, constant-speed sections, and reading holds are preserved. Springs and bounce are not added automatically. Pointer and scroll input apply only to interactive delivery.
audio: The source defines no audio. Background music, voiceover, sound effects, ambience, or silence may each fit, depending on topic and audience. No genre, tempo, instrument, or voice is mandated. Explicit user audio takes priority, and speech must stay intelligible.
assetRequirements: No specific asset list is supplied, so exact copy and task assets are unspecified. Fonts and geometry should load before construction. Gaze-following requires eye layers or a rig. Chapter transitions require defined outgoing and incoming states. Missing assets must be stated, not invented.
combinations: Product UI (style-095): screens use the same corner radii and palette tokens, #DD7353 marks CTAs, and realistic screen shadows are avoided. Data (style-097): series colors come only from primary tokens, with no more than three series and no gradients or 3D bars. Optional motion patterns are motion-006, motion-012, and motion-015.
productionApproach: The style renderer uses SVG primitives, groups, masks, and paths, with optional PixiJS, tldraw, Cytoscape.js, or Paper.js. The motion engine uses GSAP, with optional Motion, mo.js, or Anime.js, each owning distinct properties. HyperFrames is the primary render pipeline, and Remotion is a fallback only for a documented limitation. Verify decoded frames, audio sync, and loop seams before delivery.
